summary.text: Ahsen Malik, an independent middle school teacher with a background in residential mortgage finance and real estate, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Virginia's 10th District to Suhas Subramanyam.
He described himself as a uniter and an outsider.

paragraphs.text: Malik was born and raised in Virginia, according to his Ballotpedia survey response, and he describes himself as the son of an immigrant and the father of two children.

His campaign website says his professional background is in education, residential mortgage finance and real estate, and he works as a middle school teacher; the Virginia Mercury's voter guide describes him as a political newcomer.
Malik says he decided to run for Congress after finding only a single candidate on a House ballot in a past election.
He ran as an independent, and his campaign website described being an outsider as a strength and said he was running to bring Americans on the left, right and center together.
His Ballotpedia survey responses emphasized congressional authority over war and ending government shutdowns.
He received 1.8% of the vote to Suhas Subramanyam's 61.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
